principles: Substance before style — the work speaks; decoration must earn its place.
Orchestration as metaphor — every layout, motif, and typographic choice encodes disparate parts resolved into one coherent system.
Editorial restraint — spacious layouts, measured type scales, ink-and-paper contrast; no visual noise.
Signal economy — indigo is a signal colour, never a flood; a single focal dot carries the accent.
The score made visible — concentric dot-fields and barline rhythm render orchestration as a structural system, not a picture of instruments.
signatureElements: Dot-dome — the primary mark: a polar lattice of dots forming an orchestra dome with one indigo focal dot at the podium; the rising-ensemble signature.
Concentric dot-field — rings of dots radiating from a single indigo focal; full-bleed texture for heroes and dividers; drives the field-breathe motion.
Barline measure — abstract vertical barlines with beat-dots and one indigo accent beat; rhythm and structure motif for footers, rails, and content grids.
Misaligned numeral — large Fraunces section numbers split cream/indigo with a deliberate baseline offset; the 'scored' editorial cue.
Space Grotesk wordmark — STROMY set in Space Grotesk 600 with open tracking, rising from the dot-dome; primary identity lockup.
Misaligned secondary lockup — the 'scored' STROMY wordmark for cover slides, home-page heroes, and section openers.
expression.signatureMotion: The dot field breathes once — rings settling outward from the podium — and comes to rest with a single indigo focal dot still lit. The ensemble rises, then holds.
antiPatterns: No literal musical notation — no staves, clefs, or noteheads; orchestration is rendered through abstract dots, not sheet music.
No orange or Claude-adjacent accent — indigo (#61009E) is the only signal colour; the retired oxide/orange must not reappear.
No gradient floods on working surfaces — the stage-light radial is a hero-only device; content and document backgrounds stay flat.
No decorative motif scatter — the dot family is assigned by role (dome=identity, field=texture, barline=rhythm), never sprinkled for taste.
No pure-white document grounds where Cream is specified; no stock-office or AI-futurism imagery.
Never more than one indigo focal dot in a single composition — the signal is singular.

patterns.name: staff-rules
patterns.tile: several five-line staff groups at the charter grid metrics, unevenly placed (non-tiling)
patterns.scale: group height 45px at 1x; scales with the surface, ratio held
patterns.usage: background register ONLY, and low: behind or beside content on a hero, divider or section surface. Reviewed as a foreground device on 2026-09-06 and rejected — rules on their own do not carry a surface, they read as leftover furniture. Never the primary element, never a section opener or divider on their own (use grid.wordStaff for those). Set it back far enough that it reads as paper, not as notation; a regular repeat is fine here and often better, because in a background register evenness is what makes it recede. TWO RULES FROM THE DRAWN SPECIMENS (2026-09-06): (a) groups need MORE AIR BETWEEN THEM THAN THEY ARE TALL, or they fuse into a stripe field and stop reading as staffs at all — at 2x (88px groups) two per 16:9 surface is the working number, not three; (b) where type sits over this pattern it should LOCK TO THE RULES, not float above them: set the leading to an integer multiple of the staff pitch and put each baseline exactly on a line, so the rule becomes the underline of the text on it. Compute the baselines from the staff rather than eyeballing them. Done that way the two read as one system; done approximately they read as a collision.

patterns.decision: signed off 2026-08-26 (William) against a drawn specimen: the full 0.10–0.30 opacity band stands — renders pick within it depending on how much text sits over the field. Extended 2026-09-06 (William): `staff-rules` added after the multi-staff 'systems' idea was rejected as a foreground grid device and narrowed to a background register — see expression.visual_grammar.grid.decision. It is deliberately specified at a lower opacity band (0.06-0.16) than dot-field-texture, because staff rules are linear and read as structure at any opacity where dots read as tone. Round 3, 2026-09-06: staff-rules gained the group-spacing floor and the type-locks-to-rules rule, both from drawn specimens; the type alignment was ACCEPTED in the same review.

evidence.source: net-new, no external source: the derived symmetric-2col reading of website.layout was reviewed against four alternatives on 2026-08-26 and rejected; the staff principle was authored in that review and signed off. tier stays 'proposed' because there is no upstream artefact to point at — status 'approved' is what records the acceptance. The site follows the brand here, not the other way round (ORG-225).

spec.principle: staff — horizontal rules are the brand's organising device; columns are secondary
spec.staff: a five-line rule group at the charter metrics (--staff-line, --staff-gap, --staff-opacity). Running full-bleed to the margins, opening a major section, is the conventional reading and a good default. It is a device, not a mandate: place it where the composition wants it — one staff, several, a partial group, a short segment beside a heading, or none at all on a surface where it would crowd the content.
spec.headings: a label may sit on the staff, with the rules breaking either side of it and a small horizontal pad so they read as passing behind the type. Optional — a bare staff with no label is equally correct. (Breaking rather than knocking out is deliberate: a knockout needs a background matching its canvas, which fails on photographic and gradient surfaces.)
spec.columns: one measure is the default below a staff; a second column is allowed but is a choice, not the structure
spec.rhythm: where staffs structure a surface, vertical rhythm follows staff-to-staff distance rather than column count; barline measures remain available as an accent within a staff group
spec.latitude:
CONSUMER CONTRACT — metrics fixed, placement free. Renderers (deck, document, PDF) should treat the five-line group at the charter metrics as the recognisable form, and where it sits on the page as a per-surface compositional decision. Do not apply a staff to every section, slide or page automatically; a deck that opens and closes every slide with one has turned a device into wallpaper.

Of the two ways to use the group, `wordStaff` is the one to favour — it is the expression of the device that reviewed well, and openers, closers and dividers are its home. A bare staff carrying no word is a quiet accent at most; several bare staffs arranged on a surface are a BACKGROUND, and live in `patterns.staff-rules` at background opacity, not here. A single staff, or none, remains the ordinary case for an ordinary surface.

Neither use introduces a new metric: both compose from --staff-line / --staff-gap / --staff-opacity, scaled as a unit, with a word-staff's position step at half of --staff-line + --staff-gap.
spec.wordStaff:
WORD-STAFF — the primary expression of the staff device, and the one the brand should reach for. A word is set INTO a staff, one letter per staff position, the way noteheads sit on a stave. The five lines and the four spaces give nine positions, numbered 0 (top line) to 8 (bottom line); a letter sits centred on a line or in a space, and the word steps between positions as it advances left to right. Use the wordmark or label face, one word (or a short lockup), and let the rules pass behind the letters with the same small horizontal pad the `headings` treatment uses.

PREFERRED SURFACES — opener, closing and divider surfaces: the places a deck or document changes chapter, where a single word carries the surface on its own. Also correct for a cover, a title, or a small stamp-scale mark. Never for running text, and at most once on a surface.

CONTOUR — WHICH POSITION EACH LETTER TAKES. This is the expressive variable, and it is the designer's choice per word, not a value a renderer computes. It is not, however, free of grammar: a contour must sit inside the tendencies real melodies obey, which is what makes it read as notation rather than as scattered type. The four that govern it:
  1. PITCH PROXIMITY — most letters move ONE position from the last. Leaps are the minority and repeats are ordinary. Measured in the Palestrina corpus: 68% step, 21% leap, 11% repeat; aim near that mix across a word.
  2. STEP INERTIA — a one-position move tends to be followed by another the same way. A run of steps in a single direction reads as a scale and is a legitimate gesture, not drift.
  3. POST-SKIP REVERSAL — a leap turns around on the next letter. One leap in a word is an event; three is noise.
  4. CENTRED TESSITURA — contours live in the middle band, positions 2-6 of 9. The outer lines are rare and transient, never a resting place, never two in a row. (Von Hippel & Huron: reversal after a leap and centred tessitura are ONE tendency — a leap carries a melody to the edge of its range, from which it must come back. Treat them together.)

Within those, vary the GESTURE and not the ranginess: an arch, a scalar run, a near-static line, a leap that fills back in, a repeat that then breaks. Reviewed 2026-09-06 — specimens that differed only by being rangier read as random, and specimens that shared one gentle zigzag read as a single treatment repeated. Shape is the axis of variation.

DO NOT DERIVE THE CONTOUR MECHANICALLY — no seed, no hash of the word, no fixed lookup that makes one word always render identically across a fleet of documents. The tendencies are a grammar to compose inside, not a function to evaluate.

CRAFT BOUNDS, measured on drawn specimens 2026-09-06: horizontal advance buys vertical range — letters set far apart tolerate larger moves and still read as one word, and the same contour at a tight advance comes apart. Letters must stay clear of one another and of the group's outer lines. A knockout behind a glyph must never be wider than the advance, or it erases the rules under the neighbouring letters. A word that has stopped reading as a word has gone too far.

SCALE — the RATIO is the brand, not the pixel values. line : gap = 1 : 10 scales freely as a unit (the position step stays half of line + gap), the way one notation renders at pocket-score and at conductor-score size. Confirmed 2026-09-06 against specimens drawn at 1x, 1.8x, 1.9x, 2.4x, 2.6x, 3.0x, 3.2x and 3.6x, all accepted.

grid.decision: signed off 2026-08-26 (William) against a drawn specimen: five candidate principles were drawn (recorded 2-col, staff, asymmetric 8/4, single measure, modular blocks). Staff was chosen as the most on-concept and the most distinctive. This supersedes the derived spec — stromy.com.au is now behind the grammar and needs to follow it. Reframed 2026-08-27 (William) after seeing it rendered: the metrics are the brand, the placement is not. The spec previously read as a rule ('opens and closes each major section'), which brand_context carries verbatim to every format skill — so a deck renderer would have imposed it slide by slide. It is now stated as a device with defaults and an explicit consumer contract. Extended 2026-09-06 (William) after the ORG-225 website build was removed for over-applying the device: two variants were added — `systems` (several staffs per surface, spaced unevenly like systems on a score page) and `wordStaff` (a word set one letter per staff position). AUTHORED, NOT YET VALIDATED against a drawn specimen — the dimension's `status` stays `approved` on the strength of the original staff, and these two are shipped so renderers can see them, but they are pending the same specimen sign-off the base staff got on 2026-08-26. Neither adds a token; both compose from the existing metrics. Reviewed against drawn specimens 2026-09-06 (William, 8 plates at charter metrics). OUTCOME: `wordStaff` ACCEPTED and promoted to the primary expression of the device — all four specimens passed, at four different scales, which is what settles the scale question in favour of the ratio rather than the pixel values. Its home is opener / closing / divider surfaces. `systems` REJECTED as a grid device — 'the lines on their own are a bit useless… not as a main styling artefact' — and re-homed to `patterns.staff-rules`, narrowed to a low-opacity background register, which is the one use that survived. The even-stack counter-example plate (A2) was agreed to be the failure mode it was drawn as. Contour variance was opened up in the same review: the specimens were judged too uniform with one another, so the position choice is now explicitly free per word and must not be seeded or derived. Round 3, 2026-09-06: the contour was grounded in melodic corpus statistics after William judged the round-2 specimens random. Measurement that settled it — round 2's contours were 40% step / 60% leap and touched both extremes, against 68/21/11 and a centred tessitura in real scores; round 1's rejected-as-uniform contours were actually much closer to the corpus, which is why they read better. The four tendencies (pitch proximity, step inertia, post-skip reversal, centred tessitura) are now the grammar the contour sits inside, with gesture rather than ranginess as the axis of variation. The original left-anchored letter alignment was restored at William's request. ACCEPTED 2026-09-06 against the round-3 plates.
